parts.part: whole town (twin mounds Mitathal 1 and Mitathal 2, trenches MTL-1 and MTL-2)
parts.layout_phase: Period IIA (Harappan), from the end of its structural phase 2 (structural phases 3 to 5 of Period IIA)
parts.what_was_built: Period IIA has five structural phases on both mounds. The first two 'mark a formative stage of the Harappan settlement' with few mud-brick walls and thatched roofs; 'there is, however, noticed an exuberance of culture at the end of structural phase 2 when solid mud-brick structures were constructed all over the site rather abruptly', with walls up to a metre thick, offsets at the foundations and bricks of 40 x 20 x 10 cm (Bhan 1975: 12). 'The settlement appears to be planned', with streets that 'are staggered as at Kalibangan and measure 1 meter to 1.70 meter wide' (p. 13; also p. 7). The excavator counts 'the twin mounds' among the Harappan features of Period IIA (p. 15). In Period IIB the structures and streets kept the layout of IIA, with poorer walls and streets 1.50 to 3.10 m wide (pp. 8, 13). No fortification wall was met in the two trenches.
parts.excavator_basis: Cross-dating. 'There are no Carbon 14 determinations' from the site, so 'the absolute chronology for the site has to be worked out by cross dating' (Bhan 1975: 13). Period IIA is typologically a late-mature Harappan phase corresponding to the late phase of Kalibangan II and Lothal A; its start follows Period I, placed after the end of Kalibangan I (c. 2000 B.C. on Agrawal's radiocarbon bracket), and its end is tied to the end of Kalibangan II, 'about 1700 B.C.', giving 'a date between C. 1900 B. C. and 1700 B. C.' (p. 15; summary on p. 17). These B.C. figures rest on uncalibrated radiocarbon dates from other sites.

radiocarbon.context: Loc Tr MTL-1, Layer 17, depth 2.95m; sender's Sample 10
radiocarbon.note: PRL-III states that 'all dates are based on' the 5568-year half-life, uses 1950 as the base for AD/BC, and does not correct for 13C fractionation (p. 234). Phase as printed by the laboratory. In the excavation report Layer 17 is the lowest Period I deposit in MTL-1, a floor in a pit cut into natural soil (Bhan 1975: 12), so this is the first-occupation date and the phase before the layout phase.

radiocarbon.context: Loc Tr MTL-1, pit sealed by Layer 10, depth 2.6m; sender's Sample 11
radiocarbon.note: PRL-III states that 'all dates are based on' the 5568-year half-life, uses 1950 as the base for AD/BC, and does not correct for 13C fractionation (p. 234). Phase as printed by the laboratory. In the report Layers 12-6 of MTL-1 form Period IIA (Bhan 1975: 12), so a pit sealed by Layer 10 falls in Period IIA by the report's layer list; the structural phase is not given.

radiocarbon.context: Loc Tr MTL-2, pit sealed by Layer 4; sender's Sample 15
radiocarbon.note: PRL-III states that 'all dates are based on' the 5568-year half-life, uses 1950 as the base for AD/BC, and does not correct for 13C fractionation (p. 234). Phase as printed by the laboratory. In the report Layers 10-1 of MTL-2 form Period IIB (Bhan 1975: 13), so by the layer list this pit belongs to Period IIB, later than the layout; we keep it because the laboratory labels it only 'Harappa culture' and it is older than the Period I date PRL-290.

syntheses.statement: The Deccan College team, whose Occasional Paper 3 (2008) reports trial excavations at Mitathal, announces 'some of the AMS dates from the Early Harappan levels from Farmana, Girawad and Mitathal' and calls them 'not consistent and ... of limited value', but the list is not printed.
syntheses.disagreement: Implies AMS dates exist for Mitathal's pre-Harappan levels that we could not find in print.

syntheses.statement: Lists 'Mithathal (Trench A-1, 8.2 ka BP)' among radiocarbon dates supporting an early Hakra phase in the Ghaggar-Hakra belt.
syntheses.disagreement: No trench A-1 is reported from Mitathal in Bhan 1975, and the 1968 levels date to the late third or early second millennium B.C.; trench A-1 at Bhirrana gave a date of this order (BS-2333), so the attribution may be an error.

syntheses.statement: Lists Mitathal among the Ghaggar basin sites that 'have revealed Early (6000–2600 BCE) and Mature Harappan (2600–1900 BCE) remains'.
syntheses.disagreement: A regional bracket roughly 700 years older at the start than Bhan's 1900-1700 B.C. for Period IIA.

parts.conflicts: The excavator's dates are cross-dated and uncalibrated; the three PRL determinations, published three years after the report, were not used by it. By the report's layer lists, PRL-292 from a Period IIB context (4210 ± 210 BP) is older than the Period I date PRL-290 (3820 ± 130 BP) and the Period IIA date PRL-291 (3600 ± 110 BP), so the three are not in stratigraphic order.

first_occupation.phase: Period I, Late Siswal culture (non-Harappan, related to Kalibangan I), only in MTL-1 on Mitathal 1
first_occupation.basis: Cross-dating: Mitathal I represents a late stage of the Kalibangan I culture and is placed after Agrawal's radiocarbon bracket of c. 2400-2000 B.C. for Kalibangan I, with about a century allowed for its deposit of under one metre (Bhan 1975: 15, 17). The later laboratory date PRL-290 from Layer 17, the lowest Period I deposit, is 3820 ± 130 BP on the 5568-year half-life.

notes:
Mitathal (Bhiwani district) is a pair of mounds 20 m apart: Mitathal 1 to the east, about 150 x 130 m and 5 m high, and Mitathal 2 to the west, about 300 x 175 m and 3 m high (Bhan 1975: 3-4). Suraj Bhan excavated one trench on each in January-April 1968. The sequence is Period I (Late Siswal, only in MTL-1), Period IIA (Harappan) and Period IIB (Late Harappan). The layout statement rests on two trenches of 25 x 6 m and 10 x 6 m, so 'planned' describes the streets met in those cuttings rather than an exposed town plan. The report is an image-only scan; we read it through our own OCR of the locally held copy and checked the passages used against the page images.

The only published radiocarbon determinations we found are the three PRL dates of 1978, which the laboratory assigns to 'Late Siswal culture (?)' and 'Harappa culture' and which we tied to the report's periods through its layer lists; that mapping is ours. No Bayesian model exists. We did not obtain the Deccan College report on its trial excavation at Mitathal (Shinde et al. 2008, Occasional Paper 3, pp. 77-158), and the compilations of Mandal (1972) and Ramachandran (1975) predate the PRL measurements and do not list Mitathal.
